newsitem.title: USA: Judge triples damages to $600 million in Meineke case.
newsitem.headline: Judge triples damages to $600 million in Meineke case.

text.p: A federal judge Thursday awarded Meineke Discount Muffler franchisees about $600 million in damages and interest in a four-year-old lawsuit over advertising payments.

Lawyers for the franchisees said U.S. District Court Judge Robert Potter had tripled the Dec. 18 jury verdict against Meineke's parent, British engineering company GKN Plc, for about $197 million in compensatory damages.
GKN Chief Executive C.K. Chow said in an interview before the ruling that the company had not yet made any provision for the judgment. But he also said GKN believed it had a strong case to appeal.
The franchisee lawyers said the lawsuit, filed in 1993, arose out of Meineke's handling of an advertising fund that took in 10 percent of franchisee revenues.

The franchisees argued during the trial that Meineke should have simply acted as a conduit for the advertising funds but instead created an in-house advertising agency and kept millions of dollars for itself.
Separately, GKN said profits rose 13 percent to 322.4 million British pounds ($520 million) last year, but that excluded any provisions for the legal battle with Meineke franchisees.
